director.chapterArc: Mechanical scarcity opens the chapter: Callie counts snares, supplies, medicine, and days to Meridian so she does not have to name the fear beneath them. Fresh sign converts routine into focused hunting; preparation tightens into a precise, violent culvert kill, then drops at once into the ritual calm of collecting ash and the involuntary aftershock. The sight of four armed observers reverses Callie from hunter to potential prey. She returns to her mother, conceals nothing successfully, and submits to protective orders that restore a thin measure of safety.
director.restraintNote: Keep Original Calder warm, mature, and observant. Let arithmetic, physical mechanics, and bodily reactions carry the emotion. Dry humor must remain a shield rather than become charm; grief stays inside practical accounting; danger narrows and firms the delivery without haste or spectacle. The kill is spatially exact, and every temporary color returns fully to base.

cues.delivery: Give the repeated phrase the mother's dry bookkeeping precision; the wit is a controlled way of forcing Callie to face the shortage, not playful teasing.
cues.from: "Not yet," her mother repeated, in a voice that took the phrase and set it carefully on a shelf where they could both look at it. "That's the fourth not yet."
cues.through: "Not yet," her mother repeated, in a voice that took the phrase and set it carefully on a shelf where they could both look at it. "That's the fourth not yet."
cues.reason: The mother's concern first appears through understated verbal pressure.

cues.delivery: Treat the cloud opinion as weary deflection. Keep the joke dry and deliberate, allowing the slow handling of the boots to reveal the cost underneath without sentimental emphasis.
cues.from: "I am in a tremendous mood. I've been lying on a plank looking at the sky since noon. I've had thoughts. I've had opinions about clouds." She got her boots back on, slowly, and she did the left one first and then sat a moment before she did the right one, and Callie watched her do it out of the corner of her eye and did not say anything about it. "The trouble with clouds is that they're extremely pleased with themselves."

cues.delivery: Keep the loss of the mule, dwindling medicine, and promise of Meridian inside factual accounting. Let the arithmetic grow quietly more punishing; never turn it into elegy.
cues.from: They had the barrow because they'd had to sell the mule at Gaunt's Reach, and they had had to sell the mule at Gaunt's Reach because the man with the brown bottles would not take anything else.
cues.through: Fifteen days. Nine pounds of flour.
cues.reason: The supply history exposes the physical stakes and the narrowing margin for saving her mother.

cues.delivery: State the grandfather's death as a survival rule purchased at permanent cost. Hold the pain behind the explanation and land the final lesson without a mournful swell.
cues.from: One husk was money. That was the arithmetic of her entire life since she was eleven, and it only ever worked in the one direction. One was money. Two was work. Four was the number that had killed her grandfather in a hayfield in the spring with a good tool in his hands and forty years of knowing better, because husks did not get cleverer when there were more of them and they did not get stronger. There were simply more of them, and it turned out that more of them was the same thing as harder, and nobody ever explained that to you in a way you believed until you were standing in it.

cues.delivery: Place the order with quiet maternal authority: practical, exact, and meant to keep Callie alive.
cues.from: "Take the long bolt in," she said.
cues.through: "Take the long bolt in," she said.
cues.reason: The mother's protection is expressed as equipment instruction.

cues.delivery: Make the repetition firm and unhurried. The warning carries remembered danger, but the mother refuses to dramatize it.
cues.from: "Take it in and leave it in. I've watched you get clever."
cues.through: "Take it in and leave it in. I've watched you get clever."
cues.reason: Her concern sharpens when Callie's tendency to improvise is named.

cues.delivery: Land the concession and lifelong threat with bone-dry affection; no smile in the voice beyond the smallest edge.
cues.from: "It worked," her mother agreed, "and I've decided I'm never going to stop bringing it up."
cues.through: "It worked," her mother agreed, "and I've decided I'm never going to stop bringing it up."
cues.reason: A brief release confirms intimacy without reducing the danger.

cues.delivery: Let the sound arrive before the image. Narrow slightly when Callie confirms there is only one, then describe its wrong anatomy clinically—threat without monster theatrics.
cues.from: It came down the drainage in about a minute and a half.
cues.through: It did not look at her. It had nothing to look with. It came for her the way a dropped thing goes for the floor.
cues.reason: Anticipation becomes immediate physical danger while Callie remains analytical.

cues.delivery: Drive the sequence by geometry: eleven paces, three steps, brace, seam, exit, turn. Increase pressure while keeping every vector and change of weight intelligible; “All right” is self-command, not bravado.
cues.from: She let it come to eleven paces. Then she backed three steps into the culvert mouth, put her back foot on the packed silt step, and set the butt of the conduit against the corner of the concrete where the floor met the wall.
cues.reason: The prepared trap becomes close violence, demanding intensity without sacrificing tactical clarity.

cues.from: She screwed the lid down, and sat back on her heels in the dark cut, and shook for about fifteen seconds, which she also always did, and which she had also stopped being embarrassed about.
cues.through: She screwed the lid down, and sat back on her heels in the dark cut, and shook for about fifteen seconds, which she also always did, and which she had also stopped being embarrassed about.

cues.delivery: Freeze the rhythm around each observable fact: height, number, stillness, orientation. Make the raised arm and coordinated departure more disturbing through control, not menace or speed.
cues.from: It was the last of the light, the flat gold kind that came sideways and made everything to the west a silhouette and everything to the east unnaturally clear. And to the east, on the long spine of the old rail grade where it ran parallel to the road about half a mile off, there were people standing still.
cues.through: Four of them, and a wagon, and two animals in the traces.
cues.reason: The chapter reverses Callie from hunter to watched quarry.

cues.delivery: Read the geometry as a deliberate Calder-base deduction: height, angle, and the completed realization that Callie was watched. Let accuracy carry the threat; add no fear-colored strain.

cues.through: They were up on the grade, which put them a good fifteen feet above the flat, which meant they had been looking down into the drainage cut the entire time.

cues.delivery: Hold the sentence very still. Callie's deliberate hands are an attempt to contain what her mother can already read.
cues.from: Her mother looked at her for a moment across the fire, and Callie let her, and kept her hands still, because her mother could read her the way she could read a ditch.
cues.through: Her mother looked at her for a moment across the fire, and Callie let her, and kept her hands still, because her mother could read her the way she could read a ditch.
cues.reason: Suppressed panic enters the firelit exchange through physical control.

cues.delivery: Ask with flat certainty rather than alarm. The mother gives Callie no room to protect her through omission.
cues.reason: Maternal perception cuts through Callie's concealment.

cues.delivery: Allow the visible exhaustion to land, then make the instructions careful and weight-bearing. Each practical clause is protection placed firmly between them and the threat.
cues.from: Her mother nodded slowly and turned the pot a quarter turn on the coals with a stick, and the fire found the underside of her face, and she looked, in that light, exactly as tired as she was.
cues.through: "Then we'll want the fire small," she said, "and we'll want you to eat something before you fall over, and we'll want to be off this road by first light."
cues.reason: The mother converts fear into food, concealment, and an early departure.

cues.delivery: Make the command quiet, final, and protective—a permission to stop holding herself upright, not a rebuke.
cues.reason: The emotional resolution is delivered through a simple physical order.
